A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same X-CLR work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original training and finetuning experiments on ImageNet, CC3M and CC12M, downstream evaluations, and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports repeated-seed performance summaries, graph-connectivity measurements and representation visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same cross-entropy objective between image similarities and soft targets derived from text similarities, with separate temperatures. The new pseudocode and SupCon derivation document the existing procedure; they do not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Training and downstream dataset coverage remain unchanged. The new connectivity analysis and Living-9 visualization select subsets of the already covered ImageNet data; they do not introduce a new domain or predictive task.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the ImageNet comparison beyond SimCLR and SupCon to include SCE, ReSSL (1 crop), VICReg and Barlow Twins. These are evaluated comparators, substantially broadening comparison to soft-target distillation and noncontrastive methods.

E3.justification: V2 introduces label-error and intra-class-connectivity evaluation on the first ten ImageNet classes, plus t-SNE visualization using Living-9. Existing benchmark settings are largely retained. Appendix A.3's batch-size statement of 2048 conflicts with the retained 1024 in Section 4.1, so an actual training-batch change cannot be established.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends analysis of the learned representation structure: Appendix A.3 and Table 9 quantify graph connectivity, Figure 6 shows similarities learned with CC3M/CC12M, and Figure 9 compares t-SNE clusters. Existing graph-source, temperature, data-scarcity, KNN and label-quality analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V1 reports timing variability in Table 5 but no repeated-seed accuracy summaries. V2 Section 4.1, Appendix A.2 and Table 7 first report five-seed means and standard deviations for SimCLR, SupCon and X-CLR across the ImageNet-pretrained evaluations. The PDFs do not establish how many runs were added relative to v1.

E6.justification: V2 adds scores for four baselines, connectivity results and representation findings; Table 9 reports X-CLR label error 0.223 and connectivity 2.193. Retained Table 1 values also change, including SimCLR ImageNet accuracy from 63.2 to 63.4 and X-CLR MIT States attributes from 30.9 to 31.1. Table 4 updates the SimCLR baseline while retaining finetuned scores. Tables 2–3 remain unchanged, so corrected CC3M headline gains do not represent new performance.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.9 derives a cross-entropy formulation of SupCon using a uniform distribution over positives and connects it to X-CLR, extending v1's verbal limiting-case statement. The original theorem remains unchanged. The new derivation is internally inconsistent: its opening takes the target temperature toward zero, but its final sentence says to increase it.

C1.justification: The central method, generalization, data-efficiency and background-disambiguation claims retain their scope. The abstract and contribution 4(c) correct the stated CC3M gains over CLIP from 16.8/18.1 to 17.2/18.0 percentage points, consistent with unchanged Table 2 values; some introduction prose retains the old figures.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.3 attributes low cross-class label error to its selection of unrelated classes and hypothesizes that batch size explains differences from prior SimCLR results. Section 4.2 also changes its data-scarcity interpretation from matching to improving over SupCon, although Figure 3a and its matching-performance caption remain unchanged. The general limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds training pseudocode, identifies the additional baseline encoders as pretrained, and discloses reimplementation of the graph analysis. Conversely, Table 8 drops v1's '1 for same class' specification from the random-per-class graph row. Existing optimizer, projector, similarity caching, hardware and runtime documentation is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against graph-based contrastive learning through HaoChen, Wang and Zhang, and adds related soft-target work including MaskCon and TinyCLIP. It explicitly distinguishes semantic connections from augmentation/caption connections and emphasizes graph design beyond distillation, sharpening the relationship to close prior work.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section ordering remain intact. V2 makes localized terminology and notation clarifications, expands related-work and setup explanations, adds acknowledgements, and inserts appendix subsections with corresponding renumbering. This is not a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced by a pipeline diagram and pseudocode, and Figure 2's soft-graph illustration is redrawn. Table 1 expands, while new uncertainty and connectivity tables and CC-similarity and t-SNE figures substantially extend the displays. Existing KNN and similarity-distribution figures are retained with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The additional relevant baselines and five-seed ImageNet results strengthen empirical support, while expanded related work and pseudocode improve assessability. These benefits are limited by new reporting problems: Table 7's Same Class/ObjectNet assignments and SupCon Mixed mean conflict with Table 1, and Appendix A.9 contradicts itself about the temperature limit. The added evidence supports a modest net improvement despite these inconsistencies.
